absent: Exact numeric values and bit positions for dispatch queue identifiers, enqueue flags, capability bits and event counters.
Full memory layout and locking for scheduler, run queue, dispatch queue and task extension structures beyond field uses shown.
Semantics of unrouted extensible operations referenced only as shared handlers and of BPF verifier, registration and filter helpers.
Implementation of capability lookup, slice helpers, queue lookup, consumption, requeue and bypass primitives.
Complete operator message strings, dump formatting and power notifier ordering guarantees.
Batch limit configuration, direct dispatch activation conditions and kick synchronization counterpart protocol.

findings.text: BPF callable insertion into dispatch queues is provided in several forms. A boolean versioned entry resolves the caller scheduler from program context and records slice based requests. A void legacy entry delegates to the versioned form. Virtual time insertion uses a separate path that marks priority handling and carries an additional stamp. One virtual time form resolves from program context while the root based form declines when subordinate schedulers are attached and attributes misuse to the owning scheduler of the task.

BPF callable movement between dispatch queues covers iterator based moves and bulk migration to the local queue. Iterator moves accept a task and destination with flags and support plain and virtual time variants. Staging helpers record a future slice and virtual time into iterator state. Bulk migration validates flags against the local queue, flushes pending dispatch state, looks up a user queue by identifier and consumes one task, accounting for possible early dequeue before execution.

Dispatch accounting and queue lifecycle helpers are exposed to BPF. Remaining capacity reporting derives from configured batch limit minus current cursor. Cancellation retracts the most recent buffered entry and reports misuse on empty buffers. Local requeueing operates on the current processor queue under held queue protection. Queue creation validates placement and rejects builtin identifiers before allocating, initializing and publishing through a hash. Slice adjustment requests honor ownership and capability rules with out of band fallback.

A dedicated operation table serves the CID flavor of the extensible scheduler. Selected handlers for mask changes, capability updates and task enablement are intentionally inert. The table reuses shared handlers for core lifecycle and scheduling events while wiring CID specific slots for online, offline and initialization behavior plus subordinate attach and capability notifications, with additional group control slots present only under the group scheduling build option. A companion BPF struct operations descriptor links verification, registration, membership checks and lifecycle callbacks and advertises the CID name with stub forwarding.

System request entries provide operator control for reset and state capture. Reset disables the active root scheduler with a system request exit cause when present and otherwise reports absence of loaded schedulers. Dump walks all schedulers under read side protection and emits state with a none exit kind, a negative CPU sentinel and a system request reason marker. Both entries are gated by the realtime nice enable mask and advertise reset versus dump help and action descriptions.

Power management notification and deferred processor kicking form background entry points. The power handler observes the root scheduler under read side protection and requests bypass during suspend, hibernate and restore preparation, clearing bypass after completion. The interrupt work handler drains per processor pending kick lists, processes forced and idle conditional targets, then defers any required synchronization wait out of hard interrupt context by marking pending state and requesting rescheduling.

Enqueue flag validation enforces locality constraints. Internal flag bits are always rejected as misuse. Immediate dispatch is permitted only for local destinations, with automatic promotion to immediate for local destinations when the scheduler declares always immediate behavior. Rescue requests are likewise restricted to local destinations. Locality covers both the direct local identifier and the local on pattern family.

Insertion requires disabled interrupts, a non null task and ownership of the task by the target scheduler, with foreign tasks counted rather than reported as errors. Validated flags then flow to commit. Commit honors an active direct dispatch context by recording through that path instead of buffering. Otherwise the request is appended to a per processor bounded buffer with task reference, queue sequence derived from operation state, destination, slice, virtual time and flags. Appends beyond capacity are treated as misuse.

Processor kicking is allowed only for online targets, with self kicking permitted regardless of online state to preserve progress during hotplug, and only when the current scheduling class is not above the extensible class. Baseline capability on the target is authoritative and evaluated under queue protection. Preemption requests against extensible tasks validate preemption capabilities and attempt slice shortening, while wait requests against extensible tasks arm synchronization tracking. Skipped kickable targets solely for missing capability are counted, and per target pending masks are always cleared.

Slice adjustments respect ownership and capability boundaries. Callers lacking suitable queue protection use an out of band stash that applies later. Under queue protection, extensions beyond the current slice require baseline access on the relevant processor, with denials counted. Failed direct applications are likewise counted. The operation reports success even when the update is deferred or denied, leaving enforcement to counting rather than error returns.

Kicking and queue movement serialize on run queue and dispatch queue protection with interrupt safety. Kick paths acquire the target run queue with interrupt state saved and release through a dedicated drop helper before restoring interrupts. Movement reuses an already held run queue when present, switching locks when the source differs under core scheduling, otherwise acquiring the task queue. The source dispatch queue lock nests inside the run queue lock for stability checks and updates, with restoration to the original queue on exit.

Scheduler resolution and queue publication rely on read side critical sections. BPF helpers, power handling and system request paths hold read side protection while resolving program or root schedulers and while walking scheduler lists. Queue creation holds the same protection during hash publication. Insertion additionally asserts disabled interrupts. Requeueing on the local processor requires the caller to already hold that processor queue lock.

Per processor dispatch state centers on a bounded buffer with cursor and task count. Each buffered element associates a task with a queue sequence sample, destination identifier, slice, virtual time and flags. Remaining capacity is the configured batch limit less the cursor. Cancellation moves the cursor backward by one entry. Bulk migration to local flushes buffered state before consuming and increments the task count to force retry when early dequeue may have emptied the local queue.

Dispatch queue iterators carry kernel side cursor state plus staged slice and virtual time values with presence indicators. Staging helpers store a value and set the corresponding presence marker without immediate application. Movement consumes staged values under joint queue protection by applying virtual time directly and slice through the canonical setter before relocating the task, then clears both markers regardless of outcome.

Virtual time insertion through program context uses a small argument bundle holding destination identifier, slice, virtual time and flags, with the task passed separately to respect reference protection limits. The bundle allows packing of scalar parameters while keeping task reference handling distinct.

BPF helper visibility is organized into sets for enqueue dispatch, general dispatch, processor release and unlocked contexts. Each set records module ownership, a set identifier and a context filter that constrains callable sites. The grouping separates helpers by required calling context rather than by function alone.

Operation tables organize callbacks by concern. The CID table groups processor selection and queuing, timing and idleness, task lifecycle, subordinate management, processor presence and initialization plus diagnostics. The BPF descriptor groups verification, registration, membership validation and update handling with module ownership and stub forwarding.

Power management drives a bypass state machine. Preparation for suspend, hibernate or restore snapshot enables bypass to shield scheduling from frozen user components. Corresponding post operations disable bypass to resume normal extensible control. Absence of a root scheduler leaves the notification as a no operation success.

Kick synchronization progresses from pending masks to deferred waiting. Forced and idle conditional masks accumulate per scheduler processor state. Interrupt work consumes them and records per target synchronization values when waiting is required. Because waiting cannot occur in hard interrupt context, the waiter marks a pending flag and requests rescheduling so a later balance callback can complete the handshake.

The dispatch buffer cycles through append, flush, consume and cancel phases. Normal inserts append until the batch limit. Flush materializes buffered entries before direct queue consumption. Consumption moves one task from a user queue to local execution. Cancellation steps back one append. Cursor position governs both capacity reporting and overflow versus underflow detection.

User queue creation follows allocate, initialize, publish or cleanup sequencing. Placement is validated and builtin identifiers rejected before allocation on the requested node. Initialization runs in sleepable context without scheduler association, then association and hash insertion occur under read side protection. Any failure after allocation destroys partial state and releases memory, returning a negative error indicator.

Buffer misuse and direct dispatch interaction pose correctness hazards. Appending beyond the batch limit discards the request and signals misuse rather than growing. Canceling from an empty buffer similarly signals misuse. When a direct dispatch task is active, insertion bypasses buffering entirely, so accounting based solely on cursor position would undercount outstanding work.

Queue movement must tolerate failed iterator initialization and cross scheduler misuse. A null source queue arising from failed iterator creation causes immediate refusal without further action. Tasks that migrated away while locks were dropped are detected through cursor loss checks. Tasks no longer owned by the source scheduler are rejected as misuse with identification of the offending task.

Concurrency hazards include teardown races, forbidden waits and live lock through repeated consumption. Kick processing observes possibly absent per processor synchronization storage due to concurrent scheduler disable and exits quietly. Synchronization waiting is deferred out of hard interrupt context because progress of the counterpart cannot advance there. Repeated movement or consumption loops are bounded by an aborting flag that forces refusal.

Slice updates face a race between direct writes and concurrent dispatch commits when tasks reside on user queues or inside scheduler logic without queue protection. The design documents an out of band stash as the mitigation for unprotected callers, while noting that closing the remaining race would require additional application points for keep previous decisions and tick expiry checks.

ABI identities use SCX_DSQ_LOCAL and SCX_DSQ_LOCAL_ON for locality, SCX_ENQ_IMMED and SCX_ENQ_RESCUE as local only modifiers, SCX_ENQ_DSQ_PRIQ for priority handling, and an internal mask for core reserved bits. Capability gating uses SCX_CAP_BASE with preemption derivations, and denials are accounted via dedicated subordinate events.

Operator and lifecycle ABI uses SCX_EXIT_SYSRQ for reset exits and SCX_EXIT_NONE for dumps, SYSRQ_ENABLE_RTNICE as enable gating, and prepare versus post pairs for hibernation, suspend and restore to drive bypass. Queue creation uses NUMA_NO_NODE for unspecified placement and rejects SCX_DSQ_FLAG_BUILTIN identifiers.
